# Pkl 0.32.0 collection property names

This independent Java fixture records 26 public string observations of `Map.toDynamic()` property names and Dynamic lookup. The first ten authored queries are byte-identical to the separate native NUL identifier audit input. They test whether an unpaired high surrogate key remains distinct from a quoted property name containing a literal NUL followed by `property:[55296]`. The remaining rows test LF, CR, backtick, U+2028, and U+2029 names supplied through Map String keys, including synthetic-looking LF prefixes.

`cases.json`, `queries.tsv`, and `module.pkl` hold the ordered authored inputs. The first ten `queries.tsv` lines contain actual NUL bytes inside quoted Pkl identifiers. `oracle-evidence.tar.gz` preserves two fresh ordered pinned Java JVM sessions with complete raw UTF-8 and UTF-16 channels, process transcripts, source and input copies, JDK/JAR identities, and audit. `archive-identity.json` and `manifest.json` bind the fixture. Run `python3 tools/collection_property_names_fixtures.py` for offline verification.

All 26 Java calls succeed in each session. Raw UTF-16 shows the high surrogate, literal NUL name, and LF-prefix String key remain distinct. Java UTF-8 replaces unpaired surrogate code units with `?`, so compatibility checks must compare the UTF-16 channels too. Pinned `Lexer.lexQuotedIdentifier` admits literal NUL but stops at LF, CR, backtick, and EOF; the LF/CR/backtick controls are String keys, not authored quoted identifiers. These observations do not claim Java wrapper identity, typed export compatibility, Rust candidate compatibility, or full Pkl compatibility.
